reasons: Both answers propose essentially the same hybrid design: centralized policy, isolated per-channel delivery, and a separate OTP lane. Both cover the rubric fully, including rechecking quiet hours at the worker and protecting SMS retries with idempotency keys. B edges ahead on concrete, practical details: an OTP TTL so stale codes are not sent and paid for, failing closed on dedup when Postgres is down, the timeout-but-sent duplicate case, a push-to-SMS fallback-rate metric, and a clearer Kafka vs RabbitMQ comparison.
